history.summary: Built in 1150–1151 CE by Gule Bachi, a chieftain of Hoysala King Narasimha I, and sculpted by Amarashilpi Jakanachari in his birthplace, then called Kridapura/Kridakapuri. Legend says Jakanachari cut off his right hand after his son Dankanachari found a frog ('Kappe Channigaraya') inside a flaw of the Belur idol, and that his hand was miraculously restored ('Kai' = hand, hence 'Kaidala') once the Kaidala temple was completed. The striking 5.5-ft black-stone (Krishna Shile) idol of Chennakeshava faces west — unusual for Hindu temples — with a prabhavali of the Dashavatara; architecture fuses Hoysala, Dravidian and Vijayanagara styles, with a fort-like prakara and a three-tiered mahadwara gopuram. The neighbouring Gangadhareshwara Shiva temple was also built by Gule Bachi per inscriptions. Coordinates from the Karnataka Archaeology Dept: 13.3002 N, 77.0816 E.

name: Chennakeshava Temple, Kaidala
town_description: Kaidala is a village in Tumkur taluk, about 10 km from Tumkur city, amid village houses and fields. Once called Kridapura, it is famed as the birthplace of the legendary sculptor Amarashilpi Jakanachari and as the site where his severed hand was said to have been restored. The temple complex sits calmly within the village, is maintained by the Government of Karnataka, and attracts relatively few visitors. (CSV town 'Tumkur' is approximate — the temple is at Kaidala village.)

travel.airport: Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru (~85 km, verify)
travel.road: About 70–75 km from Bengaluru via NH; around 10 km from Tumkur city. Ample parking inside the temple compound.

visitor_information.opening_hours: One source reports 10:00 AM–1:00 PM (verify); the neighbouring Gangadhareshwara Shiva temple opens only on Mondays. Confirm timings locally.
